text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Party Secretary-General, Do Muoi, says Vietnam needs youth volunteers for major infrastructure construction, reforestration and anti-flood work.
-- The Ministry of Finance says organizations renting land from the government will be allowed to use its value as capital contribution in any joint-venture project.
-- Vietnam and Slovakia have reiterated their commitment to boosting economic and trade ties.
-- The Government will adopt a statute authorizing the position of a Cabinet spokesperson to provide information to the media and public.
-- Investors involved in build-operate-transfer projects may be exempted from tax on imports of machinery and other goods.
-- Vietnam has specified new functions and organization of its border guard force.

-- North Korean Deputy Prime Minister Kong Jin-tae met with Vietnamese Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh and senior politburo member Le Kha Phieu on Wednesday, and discussed measures to strengthen the relationship between the two countries.
-- The Prime Minister has signed a directive aimed at improving the Government's administrative management.
-- The visiting French Secretary of State for Francophonie has expressed satisfaction at the progress in Vietnam's preparations for the Francophonie Summit in November.
-- Ho Chi Minh City expects to invest over $8.5 million from the city's budget in infrastructure for industrial zones in 1997.
-- A major drugs trial involving police and other suspects has been postponed until May.
